content.text:
## Verdict

As of 18 Sep 2026:

- Ready to merge: [#184](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/184), [#188](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/188), [#198](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/198).
- Ready after an approval/policy sign-off: [#192](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/192).
- Require fixes or a green rerun: #183, #185, #186, #187, #189.
- Draft and therefore not mergeable yet: #190, #191, #193–#197, #199.

All seventeen heads are conflict-free against current `dev`. “Not mergeable” below refers to draft status, failed checks, or substantive findings—not Git conflicts.

| PR | Usefulness | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| [#183](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/183) | High — removes duplicated conformance harnesses and the SearchFn nested lock | **Hold.** Sonar fails at 4.3% new-code duplication. Five current unresolved threads exist, but three are already fixed in substance. Two remain valid: `build:watch` can preserve stale artifacts ([thread](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/183#discussion_r4021236770)); shared Vitest config discards caller aliases ([thread](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/183#discussion_r4021386643)). |
| [#184](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/184) | High — removes a stale 2,262-line DB lock and prevents recurrence | **Ready.** Approved, clean checks, zero unresolved threads. Merge before #183/#180 if possible; afterward remove their temporary allowlist entries so the verifier cannot permit those locks to return. |
| [#185](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/185) | High — makes PlugFn release packaging coherent | **Hold.** Six unresolved thread objects, but five are fixed/stale at the exact head. The real remaining finding is that the release gate declares ClickUp required but never runs a ClickUp-specific provider gate ([thread](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/185#discussion_r4021173189)). Also lacks an approving review. |
| [#186](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/186) | Medium-high — removes misleading AuthFn Python packaging/docs | **Hold.** Approved and green, but one valid unresolved finding remains: the Python “quick start” uses undefined `my_database_adapter`, so it is not runnable ([thread](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/186#discussion_r4021225519)). |
| [#187](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/187) | High — properly registers `@datafn/swift-bridge` as a workspace package | **Rerun required.** No review findings and approved, but JavaScript CI is red. The failure is an apparently unrelated/flaky `@superfunctions/admin` concurrency test, outside this three-file diff. It still needs a green hosted rerun before merging. |
| [#188](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/188) | Small but useful — documents the real `decodeParams` API | **Ready.** Approved, green, zero threads; implementation matches the documentation. |
| [#189](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/189) | Medium — removes nested-lock CI dependence | **Hold.** It deletes the only Node 18 client lane while the package promises Node `>=18.18`. Two unresolved threads report the same valid defect ([thread](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/189#discussion_r4031574796)). Preserve a minimum-runtime lane using the root lock, or narrow the engine contract. |
| [#190](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/190) | Medium — removes shadowed Python modules | **Draft.** Green with no hosted findings. The three package-shadowed modules appear safe to remove, but `superfunctions.schema_helpers` was independently importable. Explicitly accept that public API break or deprecate it before deletion. |
| [#191](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/191) | Medium — standardizes ApiFn Python packaging on Hatchling | **Draft.** Green, no findings found. Reasonable and focused; ready for review/undraft. |
| [#192](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/192) | Low-medium — deletes genuinely dead DataFn artifacts | **GitHub-clean.** Green, zero findings, multiple reviewers reported no issues. It has no approving review status, so merge only if repository policy permits that. |
| [#193](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/193) | Medium — removes BotFn D1/dependency debris | **Draft.** Green, unreviewed. Confirm `register-commands` is strictly a development operation before moving `discord.js` to `devDependencies`; that checked-in package script imports it. Also rebase after overlapping #180 work. |
| [#194](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/194) | Low — removes two unreferenced test runners | **Draft.** Green, no apparent functional risk or remaining references. Ready for review/undraft. |
| [#195](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/195) | High — replaces extensive fictional AuthFn documentation | **Draft.** Valuable but too large to merge unreviewed: 63 files and substantial generated LLM-doc churn. Merge #186 first, then rebase and regenerate `llms-full.txt`; the generated file overlaps. |
| [#196](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/196) | High — moves an otherwise unusable reusable workflow to GitHub’s registered location | **Draft.** Green, but its own PR checks do not execute the relocated `workflow_call`. Require one real same-repository caller smoke test, including PR-comment behavior, before merging. |
| [#197](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/197) | Medium-high — removes nonexistent AuthFn/MongoDB teaching and metadata | **Draft.** Green and focused; no defect found. Rebase after #184 and any other root-lock change, then review/undraft. |
| [#198](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/198) | Medium — cleans generated samples, imports, ignore rules, and dead documentation | **Ready.** Approved, green, zero unresolved threads. Prefer #187 first because this PR starts testing through the Swift bridge package boundary. |
| [#199](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/199) | High — fixes a metadata-only SearchFn Python wheel and false DataFn dependency/docs | **Draft; small fix needed.** It changes mypy’s target from Python 3.9 to 3.10 while retaining `requires-python >=3.9`, silently dropping minimum-version static validation. Restore 3.9 validation or raise the declared minimum. |

Recommended sequence:

1. Merge #184, #188, and #198.
2. Obtain approval and merge #192.
3. Fix #187’s red check and merge it before further DataFn/root-lock PRs.
4. Remediate #183, #185, #186, and #189.
5. Rebase root-lock PRs #193/#197 one at a time.
6. Merge #186 before rebasing/regenerating #195.

This was read-only; no files, refs, reviews, or PR state were changed.
